spec.title: Add kanban-quick command for fast implementation workflow
spec.context: The current kanban workflow (create → scope → plan → implement → check → docs → PR) is thorough but too heavyweight for small fixes, config changes, or simple features. Developers need a faster path that preserves key benefits (atomic commits, branching, traceability) without the full ceremony of multiple sequential skills.

scope.in-scope: - New skill file: `apps/kanban/src/content/skills/kanban-quick/SKILL.md` - New template: `.kanban/templates/quick.xml` - New script: `.kanban/scripts/find-quick.cjs` - New script: `.kanban/scripts/next-quick-id.cjs` - Quick task storage in `.kanban/quick/{id}/` - Structured Q&A for problem and done criteria - Optional codebase research - Branch creation (`quick/{id}`) - Implementation execution - Optional review pause before commit - Directive compliance checking - Commit with `quick({id}): {title}` format - Optional doc updates (product + engineering)
scope.out-of-scope: - Modifying existing kanban skills - Changing workflow.yaml columns or transitions - Integration with kanban-check or kanban-merge (quick tasks are self-contained) - PR creation (quick tasks commit directly, no PR flow) - VSCode extension changes

requirements.requirement: The skill shall ask "What problem are you solving?" via AskUserQuestion
The skill shall ask "What does done look like?" via AskUserQuestion
The skill shall NOT ask about "value" (kept minimal per acceptance criteria)
The skill shall ask "Want me to research the codebase first?" with yes/no options
If research is requested, the skill shall use Glob/Grep to find affected files
The skill shall create a branch named `quick/{id}`
The skill shall create `.kanban/quick/{id}/quick.xml` with combined task+spec+plan info
After implementation, the skill shall output "Now's the time to review changes if you'd like."
The skill shall ask "Ready to commit?" with "Yes, commit" and "Wait" options
If user selects "Wait", the skill shall exit with instructions to resume
The skill shall run directive compliance checks before commit
The skill shall commit with message format `quick({id}): {title}`
After commit, the skill shall ask "Do you want me to update docs?"
If docs update requested, the skill shall detect affected product/engineering docs from code changes
Quick IDs shall use a separate sequence starting at 000 (not shared with task IDs)
The skill shall update quick.xml with commit hash and files modified after commit

files.file: Main skill file using Handlebars partials
Script to find quick task by ID
Script to get next quick ID (separate sequence)

patterns.pattern: Source skills use Handlebars partials ({{> partial-name}}) for reusable components. Reference: `apps/kanban/src/content/skills/kanban-create/SKILL.md:15-25`
Scripts return JSON with tagged union errors. Exit code 1 on error, 0 on success. Reference: `.kanban/scripts/find-task.cjs`, `.kanban/scripts/next-id.cjs`
Use structured questions with header, question, options (2-4), multiSelect. Reference: `apps/kanban/src/content/skills/kanban-create/SKILL.md:66-77`
Load directives via get-skill-config.cjs, run validation checks, handle violations. Reference: `apps/kanban/src/content/partials/directive-compliance.md`

research.product: - tasks/_index: Core task lifecycle domain. kanban-quick provides alternative fast-track. - tasks/workflow: 8-column workflow. kanban-quick self-contained, no column changes needed. - tasks/create: Q&A pattern for problem/value/acceptance. kanban-quick uses simplified version. - tasks/implement: Execution pattern. kanban-quick uses inline implementation, no plan.xml.
research.engineering: - patterns/tagged-union-errors: Scripts use {error: true} or {success: true} JSON. - conventions/file-naming: kebab-case for files, PascalCase for types.
research.codebase: - Source skills at apps/kanban/src/content/skills/ - Partials at apps/kanban/src/content/partials/ - Scripts at .kanban/scripts/ - Templates at .kanban/templates/
research.pitfalls: - Branch naming: quick/{id} and task/{id} are separate, no collision concern. - ID namespace: Separate sequence starting at 000 via next-quick-id.cjs script. - Directory structure: .kanban/quick/{id}/ is separate from .kanban/tasks/{id}/. - Directive compliance: Full enforcement, same as other skills.

spec.constraints: - Must use Handlebars partials for consistency with other skills - Must follow tagged union error pattern in new scripts - Must run on main branch (like kanban-create) - Quick tasks are self-contained (no PR flow, no kanban-merge integration)

dependencies.external: None - uses existing Node.js and git
dependencies.internal: - Existing partials: directory-reference, helper-scripts, workflow-load, branch-verify-main, load-directives, directive-compliance, skill-complete - May need new partial or modification for quick-specific helper-scripts

risk.description: Users may overuse kanban-quick for complex tasks
risk.mitigation: Skill description clearly states "for simple fixes, config changes, small features"

risk.description: Quick.xml structure diverges from full workflow artifacts
risk.mitigation: Keep quick.xml minimal and focused. Traceability via commit hash and files list.

artifacts.artifact:
```xml <quick id="{id}" created="{created}" updated="{updated}"> <title>{title}</title>
<problem>{what problem are you solving}</problem> <done>{what does done look like}</done>
<!-- Files identified/modified --> <files> <file path="{path}" action="found|modified|created"/> </files>
<!-- Commit details --> <commit hash="{hash}" message="{message}" date="{date}"/>
<!-- Optional: docs updated --> <docs> <doc id="{id}" type="product|engineering"/> </docs> </quick> ```

```markdown --- name: kanban-quick description: Fast implementation workflow for simple fixes, config changes, and small features. Combines task creation, implementation, and commit in a single skill. allowed-tools: Read, Write, Bash(node *, git add *, git commit *, git status, git branch *, git checkout *, git diff *), Grep, Glob, AskUserQuestion, Edit argument-hint: "[task description]" disable-model-invocation: true ---
# Quick Implementation
<purpose> Fast implementation for simple tasks. Minimal Q&A (problem + done), optional research, implementation, optional review before commit, optional doc updates. </purpose>
<context> {{> directory-reference}}
<note>Use these scripts for quick tasks:</note> <command>node .kanban/scripts/next-quick-id.cjs</command> <command>node .kanban/scripts/find-quick.cjs {id}</command> <command>node .kanban/scripts/get-date-time.cjs</command>
{{> product-docs-scripts show_search_product=true}} {{> engineering-docs-scripts show_search_engineering=true}} </context>
<prohibited> - Do not skip the commit step - Do not create full task.xml/spec.xml/plan.xml (use quick.xml only) - Do not use this for complex multi-file changes (use full workflow) </prohibited>
<process> <step name="load_workflow">...</step> <step name="verify_branch">Must be on main/master</step> <step name="load_directives">Load directives for kanban-quick</step> <step name="get_next_quick_id">Get next ID from separate sequence</step> <step name="get_title">From $ARGUMENTS or ask user</step> <step name="ask_problem">AskUserQuestion: "What problem are you solving?"</step> <step name="ask_done">AskUserQuestion: "What does done look like?"</step> <step name="ask_research">AskUserQuestion: "Want me to research the codebase first?"</step> <step name="optional_research">If yes, Glob/Grep for affected files</step> <step name="create_branch">git checkout -b quick/{id}</step> <step name="create_quick_xml">Create .kanban/quick/{id}/quick.xml</step> <step name="implement">Make the code changes</step> <step name="pause_for_review"> Output: "Now's the time to review changes if you'd like." AskUserQuestion: "Ready to commit?" [Yes, commit | Wait] If Wait: Exit with instructions to resume </step> <step name="directive_compliance">{{> directive-compliance}}</step> <step name="commit">git commit -m "quick({id}): {title}"</step> <step name="update_quick_xml">Add commit hash, files modified</step> <step name="ask_docs">AskUserQuestion: "Do you want me to update docs?"</step> <step name="detect_docs">If yes, scan changes for affected docs</step> <step name="update_docs">Update detected product/engineering docs</step> <step name="output_result">Summary + [KANBAN_COMPLETE]</step> </process>
<success_criteria> - Quick folder exists at `.kanban/quick/{id}/` - Quick file exists at `.kanban/quick/{id}/quick.xml` - Branch `quick/{id}` exists - Git log shows `quick({id}): {title}` - Code changes committed </success_criteria> ```
